history.p: August Bournonville was inspired to write this ballet by reading J.M. Thiele's collection of "Danmarks Folkesagn", published in a second edition in 1843. For unknown reasons Bournonville decided to ask the two most prominent Danish composers at that time: Niels W. Gade and his father-in-law, J.P.E. Hartmann to divide the music between them: Gade Acts One and Three and Hartmann Act Two. Nevertheless the music may be regarded as en entity because of common thematic material between the acts. In his diary Bournonville refers to several meetings with the two composers separately, but never together. "Et Folkesagn" is one of the most loved ballets of August Bournonville and has been performed more than 600 times at The Royal Theatre in Copenhagen. It has become a tradition in Denmark, that newly wed couples dance the Bridal Waltz from Act Three.

physDesc.physMedium: Bound in black and red-brown marbled cardboard with red-brown leather spine. On the spine: "GADE OG / HARTMANN / ET FOLKESAGN / PART. / I (II) / 1.-2. AKT (3. AKT)". Written in ink. Paper: 16 staves. Many different paginations.

titleStmt.title: Piano score, autograph, fair copy, nos. 4 & 5 in the printed piano score

physDesc.physMedium: 2 bifolios. Written in ink. Paper: 18 staves. Later pagination in pencil: pp. 12-18. Heading on p. 12: "Ved Elverhøi / Scherzo"", and on p. 16: "Elverpigerne" Last page blank.

In the right-hand corner of the title page "Repetiteurens Parti". 12 bifolios and 4 single folios. Paper 20 and 18 staves. Various paginations. With a number of corrections and choreographic indications by Bournonville in pencil and black ink, comprising the dramatic plot of the ballet and directions as to gesture and expression. However, Gade's penciled notes in the margin and between the staves concern the general dramatic plot.

annot.p: Comprises nos. 1, 2, 3 , 5 and parts of no. 4 in Act One and nos. 14-20 (except the Bridal Waltz) of Act Three. According to Bournonville's diaries the notes in the manuscript were written between 17 September 1853 and mid-January 1854.

annot.p: The rehearsal score contains Bournonville's autograph notes in pencil, which describe the dramatic action, the mime, and the choreography. Act One is on pp. 1-28; Act Three on pp. 61-123. Contains many notes and indications for the many changes for the revised stagings of the ballet.
